To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the ERD architecture is a powerful tool for learning human body dynamics from motion capture and videos and (b) learning representations jointly with their dynamics is crucial for both pose labeling and prediction.

(i) the Encoder-Recurrent-decoder model (ERD) can be used to learn spatio-temporal body pose dynamics in videos, (ii) ERD outperformed state of the art methods in motion prediction in videos, and (iii) the learned spatio-temporal representations in the ERD model are crucial for both pose labeling and motion prediction.

recurrent networks with nonlinear encoders and decoders can learn spatio-temporal representations for human dynamics, that these representations are crucial to the task of motion synthesis, and that they improve performance in the tasks of body pose labeling and forecasting in videos.

ERD is an effective model for spatio-temporal data, which is a novel contribution in its own right, and that it is particularly well suited to the human dynamics problem.

ERD models are an effective and flexible tool for modeling human dynamics in the spatio-temporally complex domain of human body pose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERD is an effective recurrent network model for spatio-temporal data that is capable of learning representations and their dynamics simultaneously.
ERD models learn representations that are more effective for modeling human motion than the hand-crafted features used in previous work.
recurrent networks can be used for learning spatio-temporal representations, but the representations need to be learned jointly with the recurrent units, and not pre-computed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human body is not a simple dynamical system, but a complex one, and that recurrent networks can capture this complexity.
ERDs can learn spatio-temporal dynamics of human body motion from video and mocap data, and can be applied to a wide variety of tasks including mocap generation, labeling and prediction.

the recurrent network architectures we propose can be applied to other tasks in the visual domain where the data exhibits temporal dynamics, such as human action recognition, gesture recognition, or human-object interaction.
